utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-T, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. This is Thursday, February 7, 2008, and I would like to welcome all people from the Prosecution, Mr. Seselj's associates, Mr. Seselj, as well as everyone in the courtroom helping us. We will be hearing a witness soon, a witness that enjoys protection measures. I would like to remind you all that when a witness has such protection measures, no one is allowed to reveal his identity. Furthermore, when we are sitting in closed session, it is absolutely impossible to say outside what has been told inside the courtroom. Nothing of what has been said here can be made public. This is the rules and the jurisprudence of this Tribunal. Since we have the associates of Mr. Seselj in the courtroom, I would like to take the opportunity to mention one thing, one of my concerns. This is my concern directly. It comes directly from Rule 90. In Rule 90, on paragraph (F), the Trial Chamber should control how the witnesses are to be -- the Trial Chamber exercises control over the mode and order of interrogating witnesses and presenting evidence, so as to make the interrogation and presentation effective for the ascertainment of the truth and avoid needless consumption of time. So what I'm interested in is having a very effective presentation of evidence to ascertain the truth. The truth, in my mind, is not the truth of the Prosecution or the truth of Defence. It's the truth as it is. It's the entire truth, if I could say so, which means that when witnesses are called, the Prosecution prepares a binder with all the exhibits that are to be tendered, and normally Defence should also prepare this kind of document ahead of time in order to make sure that they can be presented during cross-examination. However, since this trial started, I must note, and we must note, that Mr. Seselj has a very hard time giving the documents he wants to show ahead of time. Most of the time these documents are not translated into English, which is a handicap for us. Secondly, I don't have the documents myself in hand. Normally, usually these documents are just presented on the ELMO and used as of the ELMO, and I don't even have them in my hands. I want to be able to hold this document in order to read it from top to bottom and in order to study it. When it is on the ELMO, I believe this is not possible. Mr. Seselj has been preparing for this trial for five years, and I'm quite surprised that after five years, we have witnesses that are heard but are that heard in a very chaotic fashion. No file has been put together, documents are not correctly presented, and documents come out of the blue, if I could say so, during cross-examination. I think it's still possible, you know, to get back on course. I'm sure it is very possible for everyone to prepare themselves effectively, because what's important, and this is what we have in Rule 90(F), deals with evidence. When the Prosecution the file, the binders, and has the documents together in the binder and asks for them to be tendered, they are admitted; but if Defence is always talking about documents that are not admitted, how can a decision be made in the end? The decision will only be made on the documents that have been admitted, and sometimes, unfortunately, for Defence only the documents from the Prosecution were correctly admitted. So as President of this Trial Chamber, as Judge, I must absolutely draw Mr. Seselj's attention on this problem. Mr. Seselj, you usually make great statements, but these statements are not corroborated by any document whatsoever; and, therefore, your words have a very -- have very little weight, if any. I'm telling you this now, but Judge Robinson, Presiding Judge of the President Milosevic case, already said that to Mr. Milosevic, because Milosevic was doing exactly the same thing. Mr. Milosevic was stating facts but without backing it by documents, and the Judges wanted documents. You cannot state anything without backing it by documents, with documents, because otherwise there will be no probative value to your words. There are two essential elements you must take into account when you present your evidence. One, you must make sure that it is relevant. When you're asking a question, when you're tendering a document or showing a document, you must absolutely wonder first whether it's relevant or not. If it is not relevant, the Judges will not even take into account your demonstration. They will not understand the point of your questions, which is why my fellow Judges and myself have wondered at times, you know, where the relevance was in all this. So please, try and tell Judges that you're going to ask a question for a specific purpose: "I'm asking this question because it deals with paragraph X in the indictment, where this is said, and I'm going to prove the exact on site." Then we'll understand. Let me give you an example. Yesterday, we spent a great amount of time on the 9th and 10th century, and some could really wonder whether this was relevant or not. We really had to delve into the crux of the matter and go very deeply to eventually come up with a connection. So we must absolutely save time. Remember, as Judges, we are duty-bound to make sure that we save time and we don't waste time. So when you think that maybe there's a problem of relevance, it's true that this is a very complex case. When there is a problem of relevance, shed light on our minds, on minds of the bunch, and say: "I'm asking this question for this reason because this is what I want to demonstrate." Then we understand, and then you prove your point. We know what the relevance is. The second element that is absolute essential is probative value. It's useless to try and defend yourself if the evidence that you're admitting or at least tendering has hardly any probative value, if any, because it will not be used in the final decision. I'm reminding you of all this because you absolutely must keep this mind. I'm not the first one to say this. In the Milosevic case, Judge Robinson told Mr. Milosevic that since he was defending himself, since he had no lawyer, no counsel, he said, "I will help you. I will give you some elements of advice." This is exactly what I'm doing, because a fair trial is a trial where everybody has equality of arms. If I find out that this equality of arms is not respected, if Defence is in jeopardy because technically it has failings, I must absolutely remind you of this and tell you of this. We're going to be hearing a witness later on. The Prosecution wants to tender a great number of documents. I don't know if you have documents yourself that you also want to admit. So right now as of, you know, quarter to 9.00, I haven't been told of any documents that you may tender. I have no idea, and this is not normal. You should have told us ahead of time through the legal officer, through the registrar what documents you wish to show to this witness. Now, maybe some documents are in your own language and have not been translated yet into English or French. I can understand that you may have problems with this, but let me remind you, Mr. Seselj, that you have been preparing yourself for this trial for five years. I have noted, as I note this over and over again yesterday. For example, there are failings in your defence. Those failings are documents that are supposed to back what you are trying to demonstrate. So I absolutely wanted to say this, notably in front of your associates who help you very effectively in preparing for your defence, in order for you to understand the magnitude of the problem. You can't say this is a false witness, this person is lying. This is just not enough. This is a statement. You must demonstrate and prove it, stating: "This didn't happen this way; it happened somehow else." I can believe you, sure, but you must prove it, not just say it. You must prove it. If this entire trial is only about rebutting or dismissing what the Prosecution is saying in the Prosecution's case and not backing what you are saying with anything, you'll run into big problems. So this is why I wanted to take the floor on notably with Rule 90 in the regulation, because the Trial Chamber exercises control over the mode and order of the interrogation of witnesses and presenting of evidence. I believe, as a Presiding Judge, I was duty-bound to do this. Mr. Seselj, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I did not prepare my defence for five years. The Prosecution had prepared themselves for five years. I spent five -- four years fighting to have a right to represent myself, and the entire evidence you have so far will show you that. I've just won the right to represent myself. It was only last year that I really tried to prepare myself for defence. Why would I start preparing my defence if my very right to defend myself was in jeopardy? Would I have done that knowing that there will be an idiot here in the courtroom pretending to defend me, who is in league with the Prosecution? You know that those alleged lawyers had in the past cooperated with the Prosecution without my knowledge, without my consent. To date, I have not received any minutes of their meetings. Second, you know that politically and ideologically in this indictment, I turned over two books to be translated for my part. You asked me to find a translator. I found an agency that guaranteed to finish the translation of both books by the end of January. The Registry found somebody, obviously, themselves, but the books have not been translated yet. I should have had them here in order to examine the expert witness testifying on Greater Serbia. I need those books. All the references are there. All the documents are there. Now I am cross-examining an expert off the top of my hands because I do have these things in my memory. You don't have documents. I'm sorry, but why would I be worried about it? What matters to me is for you to see that the witness expert is an ignoramus. He can't answer my questions. But it's up to you how you will judge him. I've told you already that I'm not interested in your eventual judgement or the sentence whether it would be three years, 30 years, or life imprisonment. My right to represent myself was my goal. We have other problems at stake. I turned over a whole set of documents concerning Sarajevo, which hasn't been translated yet. I gave ten other documents, many other documents, in fact. Some have been translated, but many more were not. The Registry is obviously unable to fulfil their obligation. I turned over one more document that I need for the cross-examination for expert Theunens. For today's witness, what did the Prosecution give us for today? Is there a single relevant document here? No. Which document should I offer for this document? I don't need any. I don't need any to cross-examine him. We'll see if the witness has anything to say, if there's anything relevant in his testimony. Don't forget he's testifying about events that are not covered by my indictment. They're not in the indictment at all. I will have to think whether I'm going to cross-examine him at all. I don't wonder that you're surprised I didn't offer any documents. Maybe I won't offer any. I receive documents systematically, not randomly. But I have another problem, and that problem surfaced in the testimony of expert Oberschall. It only escalated with the expert Tomic, to the maximum. You have seen that we heard an inept, an ignorant expert here, but he was perfectly coached to do two things: Not to answer my questions directly and rare were my questions that he answered directly, and he was also coached to waste as much of my time as possible with empty talk. He talked and talked like a chatterbox without giving any essential answers to my questions but telling his own empty stories. Every time I tried to stop him, the Prosecutor intervened telling me not to do that, and the Trial Chamber did not warn him that he was not answering my questions. You listened to every one of his empty stories to the end. I needed one more hour to properly examine him. I have never completed the end of my cross-examination, but I'm not dissatisfied. I am perfectly satisfied with what I have done. There is no real connoisseur on the earth who would say that Tomic is an expert. You can only take for granted what he said. You know how full of holes his knowledge of history is. You saw him falsify the map of territorial extensions of Serbia granted by Western powers in August 1915. You saw the things he resorted to. That's enough to me. Do you think I care whether his expert report would be admitted? I'm absolutely not afraid of it. It's an empty work with a lot of deficiencies. Another document remained here on the table yesterday that was on the ELMO. You could have taken it. I don't need it. In his examination-in-chief, he invoked the genocide against Muslims book by Vladimir Dedijer and another author. He mentioned it in his expert report. I put a question to him citing the last passage of that book and he tells me, "I can't tell you until I check." Why didn't he check before? Why didn't he prepare himself? Why didn't he read a single book till the end? He had consultants in Belgrade who put bits and -- bits and pieces together for him, but there is no real knowledge and scientific argumentation underlying his report. He is a Master of Arts under the Bologna system. That means he did not do actual post graduate studies, and he did not get his degree of master. What can I do to help you now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's start dealing with the expert who was testifying earlier. A couple things first. You know that, for the cross-examination, this is a dual procedure, hybrid procedure, but there was a lot of the British system. Normally, you know, the witness is supposed to be asked a question and the answer should be yes, no, or I don't know. As a rule, there should not be lengthy answers, but that's if the question is well-put. If you put the question correctly, then the witness will just say "yes," "no," or "I don't know." If you don't put your question correctly, if it's not formulated correctly, then the witness is not going to answer, you know, just by "yes," "no," or "I don't know." He's going to start a lengthy answer, especially if it's an intellectual that you have in the witness seat. So you're right, it is also up to the Chamber to remind the witness that he's supposed to answer the question put and only the question put. That is true. There's another thing that I can absolutely not let slip, slide by. You told us - and it's not the first time; it's the third time that you are telling us - you are telling us that the outcome of this trial, whatever the decision, whether if you're convicted, it doesn't mean anything to you. You've said this over and over again. Well, maybe that's your point of view. But as Judge, as Presiding Judge, I cannot agree with this, because when deliberating, I cannot find guilty a person that will not have had an adequate defence, because I may find guilty someone who maybe innocent. Still, as of today, I don't know what you are, whether you're guilty or not. I don't know that yet, because that will be the final decision. So I must tell you that, in the meanwhile, you must absolutely defend yourself. You must not present yourself as maybe guilty because you believe the trial is of no importance and you only want to use this trial as a panel, you know, to speak, to speak out. We are Judges, and we are here to rule, you know, to make a decision, to draw conclusions from what is presented by the Prosecution and by yourself, and make a decision as to whether you are guilty or not. This is what we have in mind a hundred per cent of the time. This is why we is have a trial, and this is why you must absolutely defend yourself, presenting your own case, presenting it well in order for the Judges to examine this. If there was a trial where only the Prosecution case was correctly presented, this would not be a fair trial, in the strict meaning of this world. I also want to take this opportunity, since we have Mr. Krasic here and I know he works very effectively and hard, remember that when there are briefs or replies, remember that there's a limit to the word count. You must not exceed that limit. There's a directive that gives you the limit. If you want to exceed that limit, you must submit another brief to explain why you need to and why you want to exceed the limit. Otherwise, your brief might not even be looked into, just because the limit -- the word limit is exceeded. There is a practice direction that deals with this. This is the way the Tribunal operates. You may have your opinion on this but that's the way things are. Now, up until now, as Pre-trial Judge, I was extremely tolerant. My fellow Judges have also been extremely tolerant; but at one point in time, we'll have to put our foot down and say, no, and reject because this is not -- this does not satisfy the criteria that are set in the practical directions. Mr. Seselj, do you have anything to add?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, at the very start, I presented my position, and I'm not changing it. The directive limiting the word act cannot be a generally binding enactment. It is a personal document by the President of the Tribunal, and it has as much legal importance as the very title indicates. It's an instruction. Nowhere in the Statute, nowhere in the Rules of Procedure are there any rules about the length of submissions, nor is the right of the President of the Tribunal to prescribe the length envisaged by the Rules. If you don't like any of my submissions because it's too lengthy, reject it. I reckon with that as well. But I, as a lawyer, reckon that the President of the Tribunal does not have the right to limit the word count. My right to represent myself takes priority over his right to prescribe such things. Why would I obey such directions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me. I'd like to answer to this. If you are right in saying that practice directions are not legally binding documents, they become so if Trial Chambers, various Trial Chambers, decided to implement them and to decide that they should be applied. So it is up to the Trial Chamber to decide whether the practice direction is to be followed or not, and then it becomes a legally binding document for you and us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are completely right, and then there's no reason to discuss the issue. You have your own position that you will reject every submission of mine that is longer than the word limit. I consciously take that risk, make a submission that is over that word count. You reject it, and matters are very simple. There's no reason to argue. It will be recorded that my submission was rejected because it was longer than the prescribed word count, and that's the end of it. Let me remind you that, for every expert report, I submitted very lengthy replies both for Oberschall and for Tomic. Concerning this expert report of Tomic, my reply was translated into English. I had engaged four renowned Serbian experts to prepare that. It was submitted to you in English. Why would I waste my time arguing that here? You have the standpoints of four renowned Serbian historians, and you can weigh their opinions against his. Secondly, the expert also talked about things that were not in the report, and that's why I felt the need to ask my legal advisors to provide me with additional material. That's why the fax machine had to be engaged, and that's why I had to present arguments that I otherwise wouldn't have. He drew the map of the territorial expansion of Serbia here on the spot. I used an original map to denounce him as an expert. That is the point. I'm responding to what's happening in the courtroom. As a result, in the course of examination-in-chief, I feel I need additional documents. You saw the same happen with Witness Stoparic. His testimony did not correspond at all with the written statement he gave to the Prosecution. Look at his statement and look at the transcript of examination-in-chief and see how large the discrepancies are. It's like those were two different persons speaking. That's why I need to respond. I need additional documents that arrive by fax, and that's how I respond to examination-in-chief. If I didn't respond, then I wouldn't need these things. Then you also know that I'm on a parallel track preparing my defence case, and I need documents for that. Why would I use all my cards now? Why would I help the Prosecution prepare for my defence case? I will give them, in due time, my 65 ter list, but why would I help the Prosecutor now? On the contrary, I want to destroy the Prosecution by saving my ammunition till the end. I don't want to help them in advance, to give them advance knowledge. Look at how many documents they had concealed from me. They had concealed passages from the Theunens report until a few days ago. My expert, Bozidar Delic, did not have all of the Theunens report when he was writing a response and a clarification. See what's going on. You cannot ask me to function the way you want me to while the issue of financing has not been resolved yet. My legal advisors are at my throat already, asking me to pay them for the last five years, and I can't do it. They are coming here in their free time. They are practically volunteering their services. In a few days, I might end up completely alone. I won't need even the telephone and the fax machine any more if I don't pay them for their work so far. We have asked for this issue to be resolved, but the Registry keeps refusing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In this respect, since you tackle this issue and since your associates are in the courtroom, let me tell you this: For the time being, the Registrar is not paying you because the Registrar is expecting from Mr. Seselj, for him to appoint, officially so, among the four of you, the one who meets all the criteria provided for in Rule 45. Rule 45 says that there must be, among the associates, one individual who meets all the criteria as expressed in Rule 44. So one of these individuals must be a lawyer in a country, and he must be in the bar association of the country. This is the position of the Registrar. That comes from the administrative UN regulations. The Registrar has told the Chamber that, as soon as he receives this information from Mr. Seselj, the money will be released. So, basically, we are on the doorstep, as it were, of a solution. This is the situation as it exists. As far as I'm concerned, I have done everything I could for Mr. Seselj to have an assistant and associates. The best proof of that is that you are here today in this courtroom, and all this will be finalised when Mr. Seselj officially notifies the Registrar that one of the four of you meets the conditions of Rules 44 and 45. There is another condition as well, but it is in my view not so important. It's more secondary. Mr. Seselj must also show that he is indigent, but that's a second step. This is what I wanted to tell you. There may be a solution, but it is for Mr. Seselj to provide the solution. Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, let me remind you that a month or so ago, here in the courtroom, it must be in the transcript, I said that lawyer, Slavko Jerkovic, is my legal advisor who meets all the requirements, and my main advisor is Mr. Zoran Krasic. Second, in year 2003, I proved to the Registry my indigency and that I am unable to finance my defence. The Registry has still not provided me with a study resulting from the investigation of my allegations. Instead, they asked for information about the financial situation of my family that I will never provide. And, finally, the Registry still has not given me information that I asked for: How many other defences financed by the Tribunal cost; how many imposed standby lawyers were appointed, Van der Spoel and the other one, Mr. Hooper; and how much they cost. The Registry now comes up with something that is incredible. As soon as I officially appoint Mr. Slavko Jerkovic as somebody who meets all the requirements, they will release the funds. They won't. Slavko Jerkovic, himself, does not dare receive money until I approve it. They have to say, "In pre-trial stage, pre-trial stage costs this much; you get this much. The Prosecution case costs this much; you get this much." I won't let the Registry buy my advisors. My advisors will be allowed to receive money from the Registry when I allow it. It's not a matter between them and the Registry. It's between me and them. It's my right to finance my defence, but the Registry will enable by determining quotas for each stage of the trial, and the Registry won't do that. That's why things have come to a standstill. There is no progress at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will look again into this problem in order to try and arrive at a solution. Rest assured the Trial Chamber is fully committed to doing its utmost for you to have the assistance of your associates. You know that perfectly well. But you also have the administration services, and that's the problem. We're going to have the witness brought in, and he has protective measures. So we have to lower the blinds again, so that people can't see him. He's going to have the following protective measures: A pseudonym and also voice and face distortion. But everything that he's going to say is going to be said in open session. Let's have the witness brought in. Let's move to private session for the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. President, before I start, I want to come back to the complaints of the accused. He complains yesterday and he complained on the 15th of January that he did get the first statement of this witness only in redacted form. We checked our records, and I can tell you that he got the redacted format as part of the supporting material on the 17th of March in 2003. The unredacted statement was disclosed to him on the 9th of November, 2007, and he signed the receipt number 104. So he got it much earlier when he asserted. But I'm sure that he got it also yesterday, the third time. Before I will start my examination-in-chief, I would ask you to turn back into private session, because I want to deal first with some private and professional background which might reveal the witness identity. I tried to structure my examination-in-chief in the way that we will go --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Before moving back into private session, Mr. Seselj, did you want to reply to the Prosecution said? Prosecution said that you received the total statement in November, November 9, 2007.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that's not true. What Mr. Mussemeyer said is not true, because last year I got a new statement by (redacted) I don't know whether he gave a new statement or perhaps the passage was taken from the previous statement referring to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please stop. You just gave the name when we are in open session. We need an order for redaction. Just remember, you have to call this person Witness 004. You mentioned his name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understood that Mr. Mussemeyer had asked for private session. I thought we were already in private session. That's why I made the slip; otherwise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Hold on. Hold on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will not happen again, but it can be redacted, I believe. So I received the statement of Witness 004 that refers exclusively to me, while the statement the witness gave in 2003 was a very extensive one and referred to a large number of persons. Only a few days ago, I received that first statement in unredacted form. In 2007 - I don't know if I have it here; if I don't, I'll bring it on Tuesday - I got a brief statement that referred only to me. So those are two different statements. Whether Witness 004 gave a statement twice, you can ask him here; but in unredacted form, I received only that short statement in 2007. The complete unredacted statement from 2003, I received for the first time yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It seems that, in reality, there are two statements; one that is very comprehensive dealing with a number of persons and another shorter version dealing only with Mr. Seselj. Maybe this is where the problem stems from.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: If I can clarify. There was -- the witness gave two statements to the OTP. The first one he gave in 2002. This was what Mr. Seselj says the complete one. He gave a second statement which were taken under the Rule 89(F), and that was given in August 2006. It was much shorter, only dealing with facts relevant to the accused. But according to our records, we disclosed also the first statement of 2002 on the 9 November 2007 in unredacted format, and the accused signed the receipt number 104 for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So there are two statements; one dates back to 2002. First question: This 2002 statement, non-redacted in full, could you tell us exactly when it was disclosed to Mr. Seselj? Then we have a second statement dated August 2006, and only dealing with Mr. Seselj. When was this one disclosed to Mr. Seselj? I want to know when you disclosed the 2002 and the 2006 ones to Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: According to our records, the first one was disclosed the 9th of November last year, 2007, and the accused signed the receipt number 104 for this. At the moment, I can't tell you the exact date when the second statement from August 2006 was disclosed to him, but it was also last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. These statements were in B/C/S, since the witness speaks B/C/S. So they were in B/C/S, and the English version was probably attached. I'm a little bit surprised here. First statement was made in 2002, disclosed on November 9, 2007. It took you five years to disclose this statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: It did not take us five years. The first time when it was disclosed, it was part of the supporting material, and we asked for this witness for protective measures, which we got granted. And when the trial was going to start, we disclosed the other statements and the documents related to this witness 30 days before trial started. That was in November last year.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I demand that Mr. Mussemeyer show you that receipt with my signature, because I assert that in November 2007, I received the witness's statement from 2006, the new short one, not the long one from 2002. So let Mr. Mussemeyer show you what I signed. He doesn't know the date when I received the short statement because I received it in November, on the date he mentions. The long unredacted statement I received only yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. According to the accused, the 2002 statement, he only received it yesterday, not November 9, 2007. According to him, on November 9, 2007, he received the August 2006 statement, and he's asking for the receipt to be shown, because he always signs a receipt every time he gets something.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I have the receipt here, and it says: "Attached please find documents that are subject to the delayed disclosure 30 days before trial as specified in the annex." Unfortunately, I don't have the annex here, but this is the signed receipt from the accused. If the usher can give it to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Trial Chamber will look into this. Show me this first. This is a document in B/C/S, but it does not bear any reference to any statement. It's an all encompassing document. It doesn't give any details, and it refers to an annex and you don't have the annex. So we're going to show this to the accused. Theoretically, in the annex, we should have reference to the 2002 statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I guarantee to you, Mr. President, that on this occasion I received the statement from 2006, not 2002. I showed you what I had from 2002 here in the courtroom. You saw how many pages were redacted in black. The witness statement from 2002, I received for the first time yesterday. Mr. Mussemeyer has no proof that I received it last November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could Prosecution please check the annex, but the registrar was kind enough to give me a document. It seems that you have the list of all documents disclosed 30 days before the trial: 0305-9433 and 0305-9466. It seems that there are two documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The document with the ERN number you quoted is the statement from 2002, the first statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So the first statement dated 2002 would be 0305-9433.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: That would be correct. This is the B/C/S ERN, the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will show this to Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Regardless of what number is indicated here, Mr. President, I claim that I received only a short statement, the short statement in November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's move to private session, since we have some personal details to deal with at first. Mr. Registrar, could we please move into private session, and then we'll have a break in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will now have a 20-minute break, and we'll resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The hearing's resumed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: To give all the participants an overview over the geographic, I want to start with a very basic map. Mr. Registrar, could you please put Exhibit number 4165 on the -- on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you can see, this is a very basic map dealing with Croatia and Bosnia and Herzegovina, but it shows the municipalities. I would like to ask the witness if this map is correct and if he can show us which part is Croatia and which part is Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the Republic of Croatia, and this here is Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Can we please have admitted this exhibit into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P165. And just to correct the record, yesterday the report of Mr. Tomic was numbered as MFI P163, in fact it should be MFI P164. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you please tell us when the first multi-party elections were held in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the first multi-party elections in Croatia were held in 1989.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what was the result of these elections? Which was the strongest party and the others ones?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The strongest party in Croatia was the Croatian Democratic Union, followed by the League of Communists of Croatia, the Party of Democratic Changes, and then there was the Serb Democratic Party representing the Serbs, and it the five members of parliament. Then there were other popular parties, the Croatian Peasants Party and others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the HDZ of Franjo Tudjman already exist?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was then being established. It came out on the political scene and won the elections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was in 1989.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The HDZ is the Croatian Democratic Union.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, could you please explain us what is the SAO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is short for Serb Autonomous Province.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was it founded? Where existed this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was established first in Knin and encompassed several municipalities surrounding Knin, initially.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later on, the SAO of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem was established, and the third to be established was the SAO of Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this later on united to the SAO Krajina or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Later on, they joined to form the Republic of Serbian Krajina in the course of 1990.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was the first president of the SAO Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milan Babic was the first president of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was he elected, and what was his position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was elected in several municipalities down there, Knin, Gracac, Lapac, Obrovac, Benkovac, and he was the president -- or rather, the prime minister of the SAO Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the ethnic distribution of the SAO Krajina was? Approximately, how many Croats and how many Serbs in percentage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, to the best of my recollection, I can say there was a Serb majority. About 60 or 70 per cent were Serbs, and the rest were Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to show now three regional ethnic -- three maps about the regional ethnic distribution, and, Mr. Witness, could you please look at it and tell us if it is correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, please put number 4112 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you please comment on this map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This map corresponds to the census of 1991, the ethnic distribution of the population according to that census.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We can see that there is a great concentration of Serb inhabitants in the south, and to a lesser extent more in the north and the north-east. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the percentage correct on the map which says that the red one where most Serbs live is a concentration of Serb inhabitants of 81 to 100 per cent? Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could we have admitted this exhibit into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P166.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I will come to another exhibit. This is number 4243. It's a happen related to the SAO in Serbia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Could we please have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you please explain us what the map depicts and if it is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This map depicts the participation -- or rather, the proportion of population of Serb, Croat, and other ethnic groups in Eastern Slavonia. It's based on the census of 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see here that the majority of Serbs is in yellow and the majority of Croats is in red. Is this correct more or less on this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can see, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to have the Exhibit 876, and to have the last map admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit number P167.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: And the next map I want to talk about is Exhibit number 876.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a map of the Serb autonomous areas declared and controlled in Croatia at the end of 1991. Mr. Witness, could you please tell us what it depicts and if it is correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This map depicts two things. The blue line delimits the territory which was declared to be the SAO Krajina, Western and Eastern Slavonia; and the line in red shows what was held under military control by the Serbs by the end of 1991 in these areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see on this map that sometimes the controlled areas go over the declared areas. Why is this the case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the result of wartime clashes in the course of 1991. That was as far as the military units advanced, and that was the line that was established when the international forces came in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One technical question, Witness. In red, as you said just a moment ago, we have the boundaries of the military control. Who drew these lines? Where does this come from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These maps were drawn based on the positions achieved in the course of the war in 1991. We can see the red lines do not correspond to the blue ones. Sometimes they went further, and sometimes they didn't go as far as the blue lines. It depends on where the military positions were taken up. And when the Vance Plan was drawn up, the international forces marked these lines on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So these military positions are which unit? Who was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the inside, there were Serb units, and on the outside were Croatian units. These were the demarcation lines, as they were called.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who among those Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Serb forces of the Territorial Defence of the three SAO territories. In the southern part and the eastern part, there were also JNA forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to be exact, you are defining Serb forces, two types, TO units and JNA units.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I now would like to deal with the SDS party. Can you please tell us who were the leaders of the SDS party in Krajina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The leaders of the SDS, Milan Babic was at its head. Next to him was Bosko Bozanic, then David Rastovic, and other less well-known people. That's as regards the SAO Krajina itself. The part around Vjestica, Macura, I can't -- there were men called Vjestica, Macura, and others. I can't recall all the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Before I asked the next question, I forgot to ask to have the last map admitted into evidence. Could that be done.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P168.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the beginning, the SDS was only founded Western Slavonia. Did the SDS also cover larger errors later on?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The SDS was initially established in Knin. Later on, it spread from Knin, to Lapac, Gracac, Benkovac, Obrovac, Korenica Srb, Kostajnica; and then moved to Western Slavonia, Pakrac, Grubisno Polje, Slatina, Daruvar, and Eastern Pakrac or Okucani, Daruvar, Grubisno Polje; and in eastern Slovania, Vukovar, Beli Manastir, Dalj, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So all over the area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I would like to have the Exhibit number 67 now shown on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a pamphlet containing the platform of the Serbian Democratic Party in Knin and the statute as issued on the 17th February 1990. Mr. Witness, can you please comment on this? What was the background of this pamphlet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The statute, in February, in Knin, in 1990, it was enacted at the founding Assembly. It was then adopted at this Assembly and became the document of the party that was being established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the reason to create this new party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because when the Serbs saw that the HDZ was being established, we saw it as too rigid, too nationalist. So the Serbs in the south around Knin wanted to establish a Serbian political party because they felt it would best defend Serb interests. This proved to be partially correct, because the League of Communists, the party of democratic changes which the rest of us in Croatia blindly believed in, betrayed our interests. The party started there. It entered the elections, and it got five seats in parliament.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct when we can say that in the HDZ were only Croats and in the SDS only Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I think so. There were rare individuals Serbs in the HDZ and Croats in the SDS, but the numbers were purely symbolic. They were perhaps people in mixed marriages. But on the whole, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please have a look on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: For the Judges' convenience, it's page 4 in the English of this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you read the paragraph where it starts with "We shall not accept to cooperate ..."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just let me see where it is. I still haven't found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's on page 2 of the B/C/S version, and it's at the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct. "We are prepared to cooperate with all parties seeking a democratic way out of this situation. We are an opposition party which is naturally inclined towards other opposition parties, but we shall not accept cooperation with any aggressive or repressive parties, especially not with those that advocate national egocentrism, hatred, or ethnic paranoia. In that we, shall not have any illusions regarding the name of the party, even if it calls itself democratic. We are prepared to acknowledge..." --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop there. It's enough. I wanted to come to the point where it said "hatred and ethnic paranoia." Thank you for reading. Could you please explain us why was it necessary to have such a sentence contained in the platform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, because in those first parliamentary elections, at the very beginning, the Croatian political parties used ugly terms to describe the Serbs. There was paranoia. They saw citizens of other ethnicity differently, especially if they were Serbs. So it was included in the statute that we would not cooperate with any parties behaving like that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. Mr. Mussemeyer is putting this witness in the role of an expert. This witness, to the best of my knowledge, did not participate in the drafting of the party platform of the Serbian political party. He can read out that paragraph. He can give his opinion, but he cannot interpret this programme, this platform, because he did not participate in its drafting and he's not an expert here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, with regard to this text of a political nature, are you in a position to give your evaluation of the text or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I gave my opinion about this document which was enacted in February 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you repeat your opinion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that the statute of that party included this text about national paranoia because that paranoia had begun to spread in the Republic of Croatia in those first parliamentary elections. There was fear and mistrust, and probably the people who drafted that statute thought it important to include in the statute that anyone spreading paranoia, fear, or repression towards others, that the SDS would not cooperate with them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Another question: This is a text by Professor Raskovic, a member of the academy. It is addressed to the public. I suppose that they're not just illiterates among them. If there's a public document, it's for people to read it, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I don't want to have this witness as an expert, but he is telling about historical facts, and I think he's in a position to give us the reasons for this sentencing in this platform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My next question is: Have these basic rules written down in this platform always been respected in the SDS in the future?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They were in the beginning; but later as events developed, the rules were departed from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We will come to this later. I would like you to go to page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: For the Judges' convenience, it is page 13 in the English text, which deals with the objectives of the party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In paragraph one, it says - may I read it in English? It's very short - that: "The one-party status must be abolished." Mr. Witness, was it necessary to mention this in this platform; and if so, why?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was mentioned at the time because up to that time there had been one-party rule by the League of Communists in Croatia. That's why it was felt it was important to abolish the one-party system and establish a multi-party system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 15 of this platform, which is in the B/C/S version on page 10, and in the English version on page 16 and 17.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please read us this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "We shall constantly take care of the situation of all the Serbian diasporas in Yugoslavia. We shall especially restore the situation of the Serbian people in Croatia. The one-party policy up to now has led to an unacceptable situation."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness read more slowly, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "There is displacement of Serbs moving to more developed areas. A large number of Serbs have gone to work abroad, and the number of Serbs in Croatia is dwindling. Once compact Serbian groups in Croatia have been totally broken up. The economic status of Serbs in those areas is weakening, becoming evermore unfavourable. "The development of underdeveloped municipalities of Croatia with a Serbian majority has become a very pressing concern. There is no national equality without economic equality. We shall use all democratic means to overcome the unfavourable situation of the Serbs in those areas. We believe that the democratic situation has been deformed."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please be aware that it has to be translated, and next time please try to read a bit slower. What I want to know is: It is said that the Serbs are living in "diaspora." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, this expression is not quite clear to me because there's mention of a diaspora within Yugoslavia. One could consider the diaspora to be Serbs living in Germany, America, Canada, and Australia. Outside Yugoslavia, as we then had the common state of Yugoslavia, I can't understand what is meant by the diaspora within Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of solution was intended?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that there was concern then that the Serbs should live in Yugoslavia as the common state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We already spoke about the SDS party which was not always united. Can you tell us if there has been a division; and if so, when did this occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The division occurred in late 1990, I think, or early 1991 - I can't tell you the precise date - when Milan Babic separated of the SAO of the SDS and the SAO Krajina was established, because he disagreed with the policy being conducted by Dr. Jovan Raskovic. Then he separated his party from the other SDS, and he established the SDS of the SAO Krajina, which was active in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How would you characterise these two different movements?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that the party led by Professor Dr. Raskovic was a democratic option. It was in favour of dialogue, negotiations, and the search for political solutions; whereas, the policy conducted by Milan Babic was more extreme, nationalist, and it was active only on the territory of the SAO Krajina. They didn't want to engage in any dialogue with the Croatian authorities in Belgrade. They dealt only with their own problems and were not interested in anything beyond their area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct if I say they did not try to negotiate or did not intend to negotiate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they condemned the negotiations Jovan Raskovic led with the representatives of Croatian authorities in Zagreb, and any attempt from other people in the party to continue the dialogue was condemned by Milan Babic and the SDS of the Autonomous District of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If I call the party wing of Mr. Babic hard-liner, would that describe exactly what it was or is it not true?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Leading question, Mr. President. Mr. Mussemeyer cannot first define the answer and then ask the witness whether it's true or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please reformulate your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please describe us, in short words, which were the aims of the two different movements inside the SDS party.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As I said, the party led by Raskovic was the democratic option in favour of talks and negotiations and dialogue and searching for a political solution; whereas, the SDS of SAO Krajina was exclusive, closed, and intolerant towards Croatian authorities and the rest of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say that the Raskovic part was democratic. Was the other not democratic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not really, because of the very fact they didn't want to talk even with other Serbs who thought differently within the Serb community. In that sense, I meant when I said they were exclusive.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can we also characterise this split in the party in geographical parts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think it's difficult, because the party of Jovan Raskovic was active in SAO Krajina as well, along with the SDS of Milan Babic, but Jovan Raskovic's party was active in the same area. But when other areas like Slavonia --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness repeat this? He is talking too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you please repeat your last answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me explain it this way: The SDS of SAO Krajina was active only in the area of SAO Krajina; but in the same area, the SDS of Jovan Raskovic was still active, and it was dominant in Eastern Slavonia and Western Slavonia and the other part of Croatia where it was establish. So we had them on parallel tracks. In Krajina, there was both the SDS of Jovan Raskovic and the SDS of Milan Babic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if there have been from 1990 onwards growing tensions in the area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Immediately after the elections and the establishment of new authorities in the Republic of Croatia, ethnic tensions grew in the broader area of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Before I come to the next exhibit, I would like to have this exhibit admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P169.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The next exhibit I want to talk about is Exhibit number 346. It is the so-called Brioni Declaration, and this declaration was calling for a peaceful solution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you please tell us what was the goal of this Brioni meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the goal was to draw the attention of the public to Yugoslavia, to use dialogue and political talks to look for a peaceful solution, to avoid and relieve the tensions that had already begun to spread all over Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you let us know the date of this declaration?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the statement was made on the 26th of March, 1991, as far as I can see the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see the date 8th of May, 1991. Can that be correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Lower down, it says 8th May 1991, Declaration on Yugoslavia; and then further down, it says 8th June.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. The Prosecutor should explain why this is the Brioni Declaration. He called it the Brioni Declaration, but we don't see why. I believe the Brioni Declaration is something quite different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I think the Brioni Declaration refers to the village or the island where this was dealt with.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this correct, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you explain us --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Let the Prosecutor show the Brioni Declaration rather than statements of the European Community about Yugoslavia. The Brioni Declaration is something quite different, and the participants were different. The Prosecutor obviously ignores this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness, please, the document that we have here on the screen, on page 2 of the English version, which probably corresponds to page 3 of the English version, you should find the corresponding passage in your language. It says "Common Declaration" and "Brioni Declaration." Could you tell us something about this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can only say what is written there, that it was a joint declaration that comes under the Brioni Declaration; nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the cross-examination, I'm sure the accused can come back to this question if he wants to. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have to intervene. We have not been shown the Brioni Declaration. We have been shown on the screen something else. That is the point of my intervention; nothing else. I don't contest that there was a Brioni Declaration, but what we are being shown is not it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You're telling us that what is on screen is not the Brioni Declaration. I have a document which is headed "Brioni Declaration." If you challenge this, well, during cross-examination, show us a document that would be the true Brioni Declaration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But on the screen, we need to have the Brioni Declaration, on page 3 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: If I may help, it's on page 19 of the B/C/S version, and there is also number 34 at the side, which is called "Brionska Deklaracija," if I pronounce it correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Registrar, could you please put on the screen the English text that we find on page 3. This is the text I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, only now do we have the Brioni Declaration on the screen. The witness was talking about quite a different text that has nothing to do with the Brioni Declaration. That's why I had to intervene.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We took note of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you please tell us why this initiative failed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because there was no interest in having this initiative translated into practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who had no interest? Can you give us names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe that there was no interest on the part of Milosevic, and I believe it was the same with Tudjman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So both parts were not interested in peaceful solutions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Before I come to the next exhibit, I would like to have this exhibit admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P170.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: The next exhibit should be Exhibit number 261.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the last paragraph of this exhibit, it says that the Serbs in Croatia lived under state terror. Were the citizens in Western Slavonia subjected to state terror?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This statement of the 30th of May, 1991, at that time there was no state terror against Serbs in Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: To be correct, I think it's a statement of the 28th of May, 1991. It's at the end of this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the last paragraph of this document, it says that there is a threat for the survival of the Serbs. Were the Serbs under threat of survival in Western Slavonia at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, the threat was not as pronounced as it is claimed; although, there were ethnic-based incidents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President, to avoid confusion, we should distinguish clearly what's Western Slavonia versus Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. Those are two different things. What is stated in the document is happening in Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and the Prosecutor is asking about Western Slavonia regarding these texts. Those are two different categories.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Prosecutor. There are two Slavonias, and the text seems to refer to Slavonia, Baranja, and Srem. So which Slavonia is involved in your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I would like to know this from the witness for both parts, if he can give evidence about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So rephrase your question. Either a general question encompassing both Slavonias or specific questions first on one Slavonia, then on the other Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I refer again to the last paragraph where it said that, I read: "Due to all that and to avoid danger that threats to the survival of Serb national being, Serb people from Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem will be forced to self-organise and to decisively prepare for self-defence." Was there a danger of survival in both regions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I've already said what I heard about Western Slavonia. As far as Eastern Slavonia is concerned, after the 1st or the 2nd of May, 1991, when there occurred an armed conflict, incidents increased, fear, and mistrust. I cannot tell you to what extent these problems existed in Eastern Slavonia because I lived in Western Slavonia. As for Western Slavonia, the conflict occurred on the 2nd of March, 1991, but it was overcome, and we continued to live without major incidents or clashes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Can we please have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P171.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Mr. President, I believe this method is absolutely impermissible. The document applies to Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. The witness says he's not very familiar with the events in that area. He's testifying about Western Slavonia in May, where the situation is quite different from the east. There is no armed conflict. There are no major incidents. Now the Prosecutor is tendering this document as if the witness contested its contents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a minute. The title of this document is "Slavonia, Baranja and Western Srem." Therefore, it seems that the title encompasses all Slavonias, western and eastern, and this is why the Prosecutor is asking a question to the witness on the conflict. He explains that in Western Slavonia where he was living, according to him there was no incident. Witness, please, this text that you have on the screen, does that encompass Western and Eastern Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I cannot know what the authors meant, which Slavonia, but this is about Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at the title in your own language. Look at the way the document is titled in your language.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've seen the title, but that council headed by Ilija Petrovic was active in Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem. It had nothing, no contacts with us in Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Therefore, according to you, this document is irrelevant regarding Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, since nobody contacted with us regarding this text that was drafted, I cannot claim that he had any opinions about Western Slavonia as well. They were representatives of Eastern Slavonia. Now, what they were thinking when they were writing, I can't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, if you want me to give you full information, it will be easier for you to find your way through this because the Prosecutor didn't provide it. If you don't want me to -- when Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem were formed as an autonomous district, it was only named Slavonia without "Eastern" in the title. Western Slavonia was not an autonomous district then. It was formed as such a bit later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will solve this difficulty by giving it an MFI number. Correction, please. We will have an MFI number instead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be MFI P171.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please resume.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you please describe us what was your relationship to Milan Babic and Goran Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, from the very beginning, I did not agree with Milan Babic. We didn't understand each other because of his behaviour at meetings where he was exclusive, intolerant. He liked listening to himself talk, and he didn't appreciate the opinions of others. He didn't particularly seek contacts because he thought that we from other parts of Croatia were unimportant. There were conflicts within the party. He conflicted with Jovan Raskovic, and I saw him as a man who was exclusive, intolerant to other opinions. With Hadzic, I agreed for quite a long time, at the beginning when the SDS was established, all the way up to the incident in Plitvice when he was arrested. He was quite severely beaten up by the MUP of Croatia, and it seemed that he changed overnight. This changed him. Then, in December 1991, we drifted apart finally, and he created this National Council of the Eastern Slavonia, Baranja and Western Srem. Our contacts became few and far between; and after the war started, we practically had no more contacts until the end of 1991 -- from the end of 1991. He opted for war as a solution, and we opted to create the Autonomous District of Western Slavonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is it correct that there was also a geographical split between the SDS members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, as soon as the war began, there was a rift between us. We who lived in Western Slavonia did not share the same options that applied to Eastern Slavonia and that whole area, and we sought to find a peaceful solution through political activity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had there already been contacts to Serbia itself, and who was opposing this peaceful solution and who was going to the hard-liner way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, the contacts started sometime in late 1990 with Borisav Jovic in the Presidency of Yugoslavia and Mr. Milosevic. There was a group of representative Serbs from Krajina, Western Slavonia, and Eastern Slavonia, where we tried to find a political solution. However, the group that came from Knin was exclusive, intolerant. They only talked about war, that there was a threat of war, and we should be expecting it. Then the incidents started in Pakrac, in Plitvice, in March and April, and then the conflict started to escalate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I would like to come to the next exhibit, which is Exhibit number 619. This is a declaration of the European Community appealing for a peaceful solution.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, are you aware of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I heard of him sometime after the war. In -- I heard it in the media, but I really saw him after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is said in this document, on paragraph 4: "The European Community and its Member States are appalled at the constant violation of the principles." The principle is the protection of human rights. Is it correct what is said in this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was such a declaration necessary at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Because at that time, the war was spreading in all three Autonomous District of Krajinas between Croats and Serbs, and such a document was certainly important, appealing to parties to stop the conflict and continue the dialogue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Could I please have admitted this document --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number P172.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One small question, please. You're saying that this document, the substance of this document is something that you learned of after the war. This document was written in Brussels, October 28, 1991. At the time, did you have radio or TV?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said I heard of this document during the war, the declaration, the statement, whatever it's called; but the first time I saw all of it was after the war. In fact, I hadn't seen it before. I heard over the radio that a document existed and there were frequent conferences and communiques.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Therefore, late October and early November, you knew that the European Community had made a statement on the situation, because you had heard it on the radio.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: I would like to have the Exhibit number 511 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This is a decision on the appointment of presidents, vice-presidents, and ministers of the government of the Serbian district of Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem, and it was published in the Official Gazette on the 25th of September, 1991. Mr. Witness, could you please comment on this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I heard that the government of SAO Slavonia, Baranja, and Western Srem was formed. I saw this document only after the war, but I had heard before the people who were on the government. It was reported in the media. They had their own statute, decision, laws, everything they published in the Official Gazette. But I saw the document, itself, only later, not during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this document say that they did not want to stay any longer in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe it's mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
utterances.text: Could we --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Judge, I believe this has to be shown. Where is it said in the document? The witness can't just say, "I believe it's mentioned," when we can't see it. If the document is shown, the witness says it's mentioned, let them show where.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I had the same thing in mind before Mr. Seselj took the floor, but he was faster than me. Where is it in this document that you can find that this Eastern Slavonia was no longer part of Croatia? Where is it in the document? Witness, you have the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have only part of the document now. I have to see where exactly it is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is the entire document as published in the Official Gazette, so it's not part of the document. It's the whole document, a photocopy of the Official Gazette of the Serbian Autonomous District.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have the document on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I see on one page, if that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUSSEMEYER
